<<76:3 notes, part 0 of 0..4>>
[MUQATIL:76:1-3/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | God showed people both paths, misguidance and guidance.
[MUQATIL:76:1-3/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | A thankful person is a monotheist who credits God with good creation; an ungrateful person denies God's oneness or assigns God's blessings to others.
[FARRA:v3p213#2/r5] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | Guiding someone to the path may take ila, li, or no preposition; hidaya means making the path known, whether the person gives thanks or rejects it.
[FARRA:v3p213#2/r6] FARRA, d. 207 · author | reports | Imma can introduce a conditional choice between gratitude and disbelief, or a paired alternative like punishment and repentance; the latter implies that God created the person wretched or fortunate. | mentions 9:106
[AKHFASH:v2p558/r5] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | إما شاكرا وإما كفورا has a parallel in إما العذاب وإما الساعة; one may omit إما conceptually and begin the following words independently in the nominative.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p257#2/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | God guided the human being to the path, either toward wretchedness or toward happiness.
[NAHHAS:v5p95/r10] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | rejects | Abu Jaʿfar calls this plainly wrong: conditional inna cannot govern nouns, and the verse uses shākiran/kafūran rather than verbs.
[NAHHAS:v5p95/r7] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | Shākiran and kafūran are circumstantial accusatives: the human is grateful or ungrateful; immā introduces the distinction.
[NAHHAS:v5p95/r8] NAHHAS, d. 338 · أهل التفسير | reports | Exegetes say God guided the way, then one is wretched or blessed while in the womb, as the Prophet related; the states may be prospective.
[NAHHAS:v5p95/r9] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ allows mā to be extra and inna conditional: 'if grateful or ungrateful.'
[THALABI:v10p94/r10] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Shakir and kafur describe the person as either a believing, fortunate servant or a disbelieving, wretched one; another parse makes them the consequences of the clarified path, which al-Farra prefers.
[THALABI:v10p94/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Nabtali means testing through commands and prohibitions; grammarians who see fronting and delay put the testing after making the person hearing and seeing.
[THALABI:v10p94/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | God clarifies the paths of truth and falsehood, guidance and error, and good and evil, as in the verse about the two high roads. | mentions 90:10
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r15] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · عطية | reports | He interprets the guided path as the paths of good and evil.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r16] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · عكرمة | reports | He reads it as guidance distinguishing right guidance from error.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r17] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · مجاهد | reports | He understands it as the path of misery and felicity.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r18] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · أبو صالح والضحاك والسدي | reports | They say it is the human's emergence from the womb.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r19] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Other possibilities are the paths of benefit and harm that instinct reveals or the completion of intellect.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r20] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · يحيى بن سلام | reports | He interprets thankful versus ungrateful as believer versus unbeliever.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r21] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · قتادة | reports | He interprets the pair as gratitude for blessing versus ingratitude toward it.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p163/r22] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | The wording intensifies ingratitude but not gratitude: gratitude to God cannot be fully achieved, whereas a person may be intensely ungrateful despite abundant blessings.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r8] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | God makes the paths of good and evil known; the person is either grateful or ungrateful.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p373/r9] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | Another explanation reads the alternatives as bliss or misery, or as gratitude from God's friends through enabling grace versus disbelief from His enemies through abandonment.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās completes his gloss by saying the alternatives occur in God’s knowledge.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r10] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | On one grammatical analysis, grateful or ungrateful is an accusative with an understood if-be clause or with an understood God-made-him clause; al-Akhfash also allows construing the terms adverbially with the path.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ says imā may function conditionally: if they are grateful or if they disbelieve.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | God clarifies the path of monotheism by evidence and messengers: a person may believe gratefully or reject it in disbelief.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Guidance here means showing the way, not creating guidance in a person; once the path is shown, a person may be enabled to follow and believe or abandoned and disbelieve.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل | reports | Muqātil takes the path as both guidance and misguidance, leaving a person either monotheistic or unbelieving after the way is shown.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid interprets the path as misery and happiness, that is, the routes of truth and falsehood or good and evil. | mentions 90:10
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ also compares imā to the alternative in the verse about whether God punishes or pardons them, yielding the meaning that He created the person wretched or happy. | mentions 9:106
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r8] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj says God showed the way as either misery or happiness.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16#2/r9] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | He calls the verse an argument against the Qadariyya because God says He guided people to the paths of happiness and misery.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says God made the paths of guidance clear to the human being.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ says both هديناه السبيل and هديناه إلى السبيل are valid, meaning that God made the way known.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p16/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās begins to interpret grateful and ungrateful as monotheist and obedient or polytheist; the explanation continues in the following segment.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:76:1-3/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | God clarified the path, making the person grateful or ungrateful; sending messengers made the proof clear whether one believes or disbelieves.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | God showed the human the path of truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, and good and evil.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The person is either a grateful believer and fortunate or an ungrateful unbeliever and wretched.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p292#3/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | Another interpretation reads the clause as a result: God made the path clear whether the person would be grateful or ungrateful.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r10] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Alternatively, God shows each person the path of his kind, believer toward faith and unbeliever toward disbelief; هديناه means showed rather than created faith.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r11] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو عمرو الداني | reports | Abu ʿAmr al-Dani parses شاكرا and كفورا as two circumstantial expressions in the إما division.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو العاج | reports | Abu al-ʿAj is cited for the reading إما شاكرا وإما كفورا; the author identifies him as Kathir ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Sulami, a Syrian governor in Basra.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p409/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Guiding to the path may mean showing the general route to believer and unbeliever through senses, innate endowment, and signs of the Creator.
[TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r16] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | God made the path clear and supplied evidence for truth and falsehood so people could recognize them.
[TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r17] TABRISI, d. 548 · قتادة | reports | Qatada interprets the path as the routes of good and evil.
[TABRISI:76:1-10#6/r18] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The path can mean knowledge of religion through reason and revelation, which every accountable person must follow to attain eternal reward.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | God made the path of guidance clear through proofs and by sending a messenger.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p428#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ explains that God made the path clear, whether the person is grateful or unbelieving.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After forming the human and giving outward and inward faculties, God made the paths of guidance and error clear.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The senses precede intellect in existence: perception yields basic judgments such as non-contradiction and the whole being greater than its part, which reasoning then uses to reach unknown conclusions.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | If hearing and sight mean intellect, the first verse says intellect was given so that the path and what must or must not be done could be known.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Sabīl may mean the routes of good and evil, salvation and ruin; the singular is generic, and God has identified and explained both. | mentions 90:10, 103:2
[RAZI-FULL:v30p210#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Alternatively, sabīl means only the path of guidance,
<<part 0 ends; continues in part 1>>

 the path deserving that name absolutely; a path of error is named only relationally. | mentions 33:67
[RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Guiding to the path means creating signs, guiding intellect, sending prophets, and revealing books; it does not mean creating actual guidance, but showing the route. | mentions 8:42
[RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ says the verb may be used with “the path,” “to the path,” or “for the path.”
[RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | One parsing makes grateful and ungrateful circumstantial states of the human: God's direction is complete in either belief or disbelief.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Another parsing supplies an omitted kāna: whether he was grateful or ungrateful.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A third reads the guidance as enabling a distinction between gratitude and disbelief, obedience and sin, as in verses about testing people's deeds. | mentions 11:7, 29:3, 47:31
[RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · القفال | reports | Al-Qaffāl compares the omitted conditional fa to saying, “I advised you; if you wish, accept, and if you wish, leave it.”
[RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | The wording may also be a warning: choose belief or disbelief, for God has prepared the fitting outcome for each. | mentions 18:29
[RAZI-FULL:v30p211/r8] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A fourth parsing treats grateful and ungrateful as circumstantial descriptions of the path itself, a figurative attribution.
[QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r11] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | God showed humanity guidance and error through messengers, as also said at 90:10. | mentions 90:10
[QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says the path is the way to misery or felicity.
[QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الضحاك وأبو صالح والسدي | reports | Al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi interpret the path as a person's exit from the womb.
[QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r14] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Another view takes the path as benefits and harms recognized through instinct and developed reason.
[QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r15] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الفراء | prefers | The Kufans take in as a conditional particle with redundant ma, a reading al-Farra prefers; Basrans object that a noun needs an implied verb.
[QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r16] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Another explanation says God showed proofs of monotheism; faith follows if He creates guidance, and unbelief if He abandons a person.
[QURTUBI-FULL:76:2-3/r17] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الماوردي | reports | Al-Mawardi explains the word choice: human gratitude is not intensive because God's favors cannot be repaid, while human disbelief is abundant.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | God showed humanity the path by setting out proofs and sending down signs.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Thankful and ungrateful are two states of the human referent: all are shown the path, then some follow it and some turn away; alternatively they qualify the path figuratively.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:76:3-4/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | A reading with fatḥ on ammā omits the response; ungrateful rather than unbelieving preserves the rhyme and signals widespread ingratitude, though culpability lies in deep indulgence.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | God showed the path of guidance through rational proofs and revealed evidence.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Thankful means believing and ungrateful means disbelieving; these may be circumstantial descriptions of the person guided.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Alternatively, the path itself is figuratively described as a thankful path or an ungrateful path.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p302#4/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | After naming the two groups, the text follows with what God prepared for each.
[QASHANI:76:3-6/r1] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | God guides by rational and transmitted proofs; grateful people use their faculties for obedience and reaching the Benefactor, while the ungrateful are veiled by blessings and misuse them.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | God guided humanity by showing the road and the outcomes of guidance and destruction.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مجاهد والسدي | reports | Mujahid says the path is the way to felicity or misery; al-Suddi says it is the route out of the womb.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari says God enabled both possibilities and invited people to Islam through rational and transmitted proofs, so belief or unbelief establishes responsibility.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو السمال وأبو العاج | reports | While most read imma with kasra, Abu al-Sammal and Abu al-ʿAj open both instances, a dialect reported by Abu Zayd and also used as a coordinating particle.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari says gratitude comes by God’s enabling, while ingratitude comes from bad choice.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Shakiran and kafuran are circumstantial phrases from the object pronoun in ‘We guided him’; an alternative makes them describe the two paths metaphorically.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari also allows the adjectives to qualify the two paths, metaphorically describing them as grateful or ungrateful. | mentions 90:10
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p359/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Shakir is not intensified because gratitude is rare, while kafur is intensified because unbelief is common.
[SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | شاكرًا is an accusative circumstantial phrase qualifying the object of هديناه, meaning He showed the person both possible states; Abu al-Baqa allows a prospective state.
[SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Alternatively the circumstantial phrase qualifies السبيل metaphorically, as in هديناه النجدين; the path is called grateful or ungrateful. | mentions 90:10
[SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The common kasra reading of إما makes it synonymous with أو; grammarians have previously differed on its analysis.
[SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · مكي | reports | He transmits the Kufan view that إما is conditional إن plus ما, but Basrans reject it because إن does not govern nouns without an implied verb. | mentions 9:6
[SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | The author rejects the objection that an implied verb would force شاكرًا into nominative; one can supply a verb governing it in the accusative.
[SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو السمال وأبو العجاج | reports | They read إما with fatḥa; it can be the coordinating conjunction in a dialect, as attested by poetry, or the detailed أما construction with an omitted response.
[SAMIN-DURR:76:3/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | For the detailed reading, he supplies an omitted contrast: gratitude comes through divine enabling, while disbelief comes from the person's bad choice.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God clarified the paths of good and evil, like guiding Thamud and showing the two paths. | mentions 41:17, 90:10
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عكرمة وعطية وابن زيد ومجاهد والجمهور | prefers | The well-known majority interpretation is that God made the way clear; Ibn Kathir calls this the correct view.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · مجاهد وأبو صالح والضحاك والسدي | rejects | An unusual alternative takes guidance as emergence from the womb; Ibn Kathir rejects it in favor of the popular interpretation.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | ‘Grateful or ungrateful’ is an accusative circumstantial phrase describing the person guided, meaning ultimately happy or wretched.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو مالك الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Everyone begins the day either ruining or freeing himself; Muslim transmits the report.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Every newborn is on the innate disposition until speech develops, then is grateful or ungrateful; Ibn Kathir links this to the verse on primordial nature. | mentions 30:30
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Each person leaving home is followed by an angel’s or Satan’s banner, depending on whether the purpose pleases or angers God.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r8] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet warns Ka'b ibn Ujra about misguided rulers: endorsing their lies or assisting oppression disowns a person, while refusing both keeps him with the Prophet and his Pond.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p286/r9] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The same report calls fasting a shield, charity an eraser of sin, prayer a قربان or proof, and warns that flesh nourished by illicit earnings belongs in Hell.
[BURHAN:v2p513/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · عبد الجبار بن أحمد | reports | Answering Sahib ibn Abbad, Abd al-Jabbar says each act of thanks is small against God's many gifts, while each act of ingratitude is great; hence شاكرا versus emphatic كفورا.
[BURHAN:v4p244/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · صاحب الأزهية | reports | The Azhiyya author says this use ordinarily repeats إما; repetition can be omitted when a substitute such as إلا o

ccurs in the other clause.
[BURHAN:v4p244/r5] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | إما can express indeterminacy, as in whether God punishes or relents, and also occurs in nonrepeated conditional constructions built from إن plus redundant ما. | mentions 48:29
[BURHAN:v4p244/r6] BURHAN, d. 794 · البصريون | reports | The Basrans read إما here as choice and parse شاكرا and كفورا as accusative circumstantial phrases.
[BURHAN:v4p244/r7] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | reports | Other analyses say the choice concerns God’s declaration that He does what He wills, or treat the states as signs: gratitude signals felicity and disbelief misery.
[BURHAN:v4p244/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · الكوفيون | reports | The Kufans allow a conditional reading, meaning whether the person is grateful or ungrateful; Makkī rejects it because a conditional إن does not govern a noun here without an omitted verb, which would wrongly make شاكر nominative.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p260/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Biqāʿī places the passage after the deniers’ prideful rejection of resurrection, contrasting that posture with reflection on humanity’s humble origin. | mentions 75:3, 75:31, 75:32, 75:33, 75:37, 75:38
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The Creator formed varied bones, joints, tendons, and ligaments, specifying their shapes and counts so the body can move and remain sound.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Distinct senses and organs serve precise purposes: eyes convey images, ears gather sound, the nose detects scents, teeth divide food, and the tongue expresses thought.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Internal organs divide the work of digestion and circulation; the entire intricate body begins as a tiny drop in three layers of darkness, proving its unseen Maker.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p261/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | People marvel at a fine design on a wall yet overlook the Creator of the far greater wonders in themselves and others.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God guides by making the clear path known through revealed books, messengers, signs within and beyond the self, and insight that distinguishes truth from falsehood and divine speech from human speech.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The two human outcomes are thankfulness and ingratitude: shākir is an unmarked active participle because no one can fully thank every blessing, while kafūr is intensive because people can become deeply ungrateful, even by denying one favor.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Thankfulness is named first as the human norm and because mercy precedes anger; ingratitude includes turning away, denial, worship of others, and stubbornness.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p264/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet says every child is born upon the fiṭrah, after which parents make the child Jewish, Christian, or Magian; the author cites versions transmitted from Abū Hurayrah, Ibn ʿAbbās, Jābir, and al-Aswad ibn Surayʿ.
[DURR-FULL:v8p367/r14] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · قتادة | reports | Qatada traces development from drop through clot, lump, bone, flesh, and hair; God explains origins to test gratitude and knowledge of His rights, then guides people to gratitude or ingratitude. | mentions 23:14
[DURR-FULL:v8p368/r3] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · عكرمة | reports | 'We guided him to the way' means guidance to the path.
[DURR-FULL:v8p368/r4] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · مجاهد | reports | The way comprises felicity and wretchedness.
[DURR-FULL:v8p368/r5] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · عطية العوفي | reports | The way is good and evil.

[ALUSI-FULL:v29p153/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | “Thankful or ungrateful” may describe two states of the same person, since the path is shown in either state, or divide people: some follow truth gratefully and others reject it arrogantly.
